input.quote: The Servicer will indemnify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (including in its capacity as Note Paying Agent), and their officers, directors, employees and agents (each, an "Indemnified Person") for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees and expenses) resulting from the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents
input.rationale: Section 6.3 runs in our favour but is textually short of the preferred position on five counts: the indemnity is not an express duty to defend (Section 6.3(b) is permissive - the Servicer "may participate in and assume the defense"), the Indemnified Person definition reaches the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and their officers, directors, employees and agents but not the Issuer's Affiliates, and the triggers are exhaustively "willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence", with no violation-of-Law, data-breach or intellectual-property-infringement limb, and no cooperation covenant. We have repaired each in the shortest operative form: "will defend and indemnify" plus "and its Affiliates" in Section 6.3(a)(i) and "will defend and indemnify" in (a)(ii); a new (a)(iii) adding violation of Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data or Receivable Files (Cellco acts as Custodian of the Receivable Files), and third-party IP infringement or misappropriation claims for services or deliverables provided under the Transaction Documents; and a reasonable-cooperation sentence after the defence-assumption mechanics. We deliberately did not touch the permissive assumption of defence in Section 6.3(b), because it allocates control of the defence and the conditional mechanics in the following paragraph ("If the Servicer ... notifies the Indemnified Person of its intention to assume the defense") depend on it. We also did not import the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap - Section 6.3 is presently uncapped, which is better for us - and we added no Issuer or Depositor indemnity, since none exists today (Section 9.2 is a narrow defence-of-title covenant). If the business confirms the transaction has no services, deliverables, software or IP-licence subject matter, limb (C) can be dropped as scoped out.

proposal.summary: Make Cellco's Section 6.3 indemnity a defence obligation running to the Issuer's Affiliates and add limbs for violation of Law, data breach and IP infringement, plus a cooperation sentence.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made Cellco's Section 6.3 indemnity an express duty to defend, extended the Indemnified Persons to the Issuer's Affiliates, and added limbs for violation of Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data or Receivable Files, and third-party intellectual property infringement claims, with a reasonable-cooperation sentence in the Proceedings mechanics. The existing notice, defence-control and settlement provisions and the uncapped nature of the indemnity are unchanged; we have not added any Issuer or Depositor indemnity.

ops.oldText: The Servicer will indemnify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee
ops.newText: The Servicer will defend and indemnify the Issuer and its Affiliates, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee

ops.oldText: The Marketing Agent will indemnify the Indemnified Persons
ops.newText: The Marketing Agent will defend and indemnify the Indemnified Persons

ops.text: Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent will also defend and indemnify the Indemnified Persons for such amounts resulting from (A) its violation of applicable Law, (B) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data or Receivable Files caused by it (including the Servicer in its capacity as Custodian) or (C) any claim that any services or deliverables it provides under the Transaction Documents infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.
The Indemnified Person will provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of the Proceeding.
